summary.headline: Shriram Properties Q2 FY27 PAT rose to Rs 21.6 crore from Rs 8.6 crore, with sales of Rs 580-583 crore and FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 1,300-1,500 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 sales of about Rs 580-583 crore, up about 20% QoQ, with collections of Rs 431 crore (up 18% QoQ). Q2 revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs 272 crore and EBITDA rose to Rs 62 crore from Rs 19 crore, with the margin around 23%. The company converted five JVs (three projects) into wholly owned subsidiaries, which raised reported debt to Rs 1,118 crore and net debt to Rs 761 crore, with net debt/equity moving from about 0.29 to 0.51. Management reiterated FY27 guidance but said revenue recognition will be heavily weighted to H2, and it reiterated (with some ambiguity on the slide) the FY28 mission of Rs 5,000 crore sales and Rs 2,500 crore revenue.

segments.name: Kolkata
segments.commentary: Accounts for about 50% of H1 revenue per management. Plotted development launched late 2025 reportedly about 75% sold; management cites contribution of Rs 6-8 crore per acre before land cost.

segments.name: Bangalore, Chennai, Pune
segments.commentary: Launches in Chennai and Kolkata in H1. Pune's Manjari (2.3 million sq ft, integrated township) has received environmental clearance and is expected to launch around Nov-Dec 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance: management said Rs 1,300-1,500 crore, later revised to Rs 1,500-1,600 crore in the Q&A; treat the range as unclear.
FY27 EBITDA guidance of about Rs 300 crore; margin on revenue about 20% (later cited as 8-10% in a follow-up answer, inconsistent with the EBITDA figure).
FY27 launch calendar of about 5.93 million sq ft; about 5.25 million sq ft planned to launch in the year. Chennai GDU project targeted for Q4; Pune Mangiri moved from Q2 to Q3.
FY28 mission targets (not in the presentation): sales Rs 5,000 crore, revenue Rs 2,500 crore, PAT about Rs 250 crore; management said the slide would be re-uploaded.
Net debt/equity comfort level stated as up to 0.75, with an aim to stay below 0.5; incremental net debt additions of no more than about Rs 250 crore expected before March 2027.

Business development: 8-9 million sq ft (about Rs 7,500-8,000 crore GDV) at documentation stage, with 21 projects under evaluation; management expects press releases in coming weeks. Aim to nearly double the upcoming pipeline in 15-24 months.
capex_capacity: Ongoing portfolio about 15.5 million sq ft, of which about 13.3 million sq ft sold; unsold GDV on ongoing projects about Rs 1,400 crore, and about Rs 11,560 crore on upcoming projects.

Handover pipeline: 1,450 units handed over in H1; more than 2,200 additional handovers expected in H2, with revenue potential of about Rs 1,100-1,200 crore; key projects 1,07 South-East (about 796 pending units) and Sunshine 2 (about 776 pending units).

Restructuring: five JVs (three projects) converted to wholly owned subsidiaries, moving from equity-accounted share of profit to full line-by-line consolidation. Management estimated about Rs 1,800 crore of additional revenue recognition potential from these projects.

Kolkata land bank of about 105-130 acres (net developable about 130-150 acres after 40 acres to government); plan to monetise via plots and villas over 3-5 years, valued by management at Rs 1,800-2,000 crore of cash flow.
demand_pricing: Management said market demand is better, citing Anarock data showing a sequential recovery in Sept quarter; Pune cited at about 20% QoQ growth.

Villas (4-5 bedroom sold in 30 days; 3-bedroom ticket about Rs 1.6 crore after price increase) in Kolkata demonstrated stronger absorption than apartments, which management had believed were capped at Rs 70-75 lakh tickets.

Cost inflation: management said current increases are within long-term trends, with a buffer in budgeting and fixed-price contracts with cost escalation provisions; targets a margin band of about 30-35% (also referred to as mid-20s in the call).
Acquisition hurdle IRR of at least 25% for new projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 revenue and PBT outlook, and the debt trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave FY27 revenue of Rs 1,300-1,500 crore (later Rs 1,500-1,600 crore), EBITDA of about Rs 300 crore, and said net debt could rise by no more than about Rs 250 crore before March 2027, with a comfort ceiling of 0.75x.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the JV partner (landowner) exiting, and what is the financial impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The landowner's role had become limited and it wants to pursue new parcels. The company said it paid Rs 237 crore (Rs 200 crore assumed JV debt plus Rs 37 crore consideration) for the three JVs and Rs 100 crore to the AIF partner for exit, adding about Rs 300 crore of debt; management claimed about Rs 150 crore of value accretion after cost of funds.

qa_highlights.question: Why were FY28 targets missing from the presentation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the slide was changed because of a deeper review of the pipeline; it said the FY28 mission of Rs 5,000 crore sales and Rs 2,500 crore revenue stands, and cited Rs 4,600 crore of revenue potential from completed projects plus about Rs 15,000 crore from signed contracts. The slide will be re-uploaded.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the YoY revenue down and the new project investment line only Rs 17 crore in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 launches were planned to be weighted to H2 by design; the Rs 105 crore H1 new project investment covers BD-related payments only, while construction spend sits in operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kolkata monetisation strategy versus outright sale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is pursuing development-led monetisation of about 105-130 acres via plots and villas, targeting Rs 600-700 crore of contribution over 3-5 years, and is open to bulk sales or JDAs if NPV is comparable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing and scale of the Mumbai/MMR entry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is evaluating multiple MMR micro markets and other markets, but declined to name micro markets or size until transactions are signed, expected this quarter or next.

risks_watch: Revenue recognition heavily back-ended: H1 revenue about Rs 543 crore; FY27 guidance of Rs 1,300-1,600 crore needs about Rs 760-1,060 crore in H2 and depends on OCs, approvals and completions.
Balance sheet: gross debt rose to Rs 1,118 crore from Rs 851 crore, and net debt to Rs 761 crore; ratio at 0.51 with management tolerance up to 0.75.
Project execution risk: about 6 million sq ft of development rights with signed contracts lack approved plans; management said these are being worked on.
Launch slippage: Pune Mangiri moved from Q2 to Q3 and some Chennai and Bangalore launches are pending; about 5.25 million sq ft planned for FY27.
Inconsistent figures in the transcript (net debt Rs 161 crore vs Rs 761 crore, FY27 revenue range, margin 8-10% vs 20-23%, and H1 PAT); verify against filed results.
Late filing of the presentation was due to an Outlook outage; the FY28 slide was removed and may be re-uploaded.

summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, sales momentum, cash flow and the FY27 launch and handover pipeline, but cautious and somewhat defensive on the FY28 target, which was dropped from the slide deck and reinstated verbally. Answers on FY27 revenue, EBITDA and margin were inconsistent and corrected several times, and management was evasive on the Mumbai/MMR micro markets and the JV economics.

adds.what: Pune Manjari integrated township (2.3 million sq ft) launch, environmental clearance received; expected launch around Nov-Dec 2026
FY27 launch calendar of about 5.25 million sq ft planned to launch in the year (Chennai GDU targeted Q4; Pune Mangiri moved Q2 to Q3)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance is unclear (Rs 1,300-1,500 cr in the deck, verbally revised to Rs 1,500-1,600 cr) and FY27 EBITDA is held at about Rs 300 cr; delivery rests on a 5.25 mn sq ft launch calendar, about Rs 1,100-1,200 cr of H2 handover potential and the five-JV consolidation (about Rs 1,800 cr revenue potential), with H2-weighted recognition, but no firm numbers on revenue timing.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin about 23% (Rs 62 crore on Rs 272 crore revenue) versus about 8% a year earlier, FY27 EBITDA guided at about Rs 300 crore, and management targets a 30-35% margin band, though the call also cited mid-20s and an 8-10% figure, so the level is unclear.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: FY27 launch calendar is about 5.25 million sq ft out of 5.93 million sq ft planned; Pune Manjari (2.3 million sq ft) has environmental clearance for a Nov-Dec 2026 launch, Chennai GDU is targeted for Q4 and Pune Mangiri has slipped from Q2 to Q3.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 sales were about 0.91 million sq ft and H1 about 1.76 million sq ft, with management citing a sequential demand recovery (Pune about 20% QoQ) and more than 2,200 handovers expected in H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management has not guided a capex plan, but a Kolkata land bank of 105-130 acres is planned for plots and villas over 3-5 years and business development of 8-9 million sq ft is at documentation stage, so land or project commitments are likely rather than factory capex.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance is unclear (Rs 1,300-1,500 crore in the deck, verbally Rs 1,500-1,600 crore) and needs about Rs 760-1,060 crore in H2 against H1 revenue of about Rs 543 crore, so an upgrade is not supported yet.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue recognition is heavily back-ended and depends on OCs and approvals, with Pune Mangiri already slipping from Q2 to Q3, and about 6 million sq ft of signed development rights still lack approved plans.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pune Manjari integrated township (2.3 million sq ft) is expected to launch around Nov-Dec 2026, and Kolkata villas (3-bedroom ticket about Rs 1.6 crore) showed faster absorption than apartments.

rows.label: Five JVs consolidated; about Rs 1,800 crore revenue recognition potential
rows.why: Conversion of five JVs (three projects) to wholly owned subsidiaries moves them to line-by-line consolidation, with management estimating about Rs 1,800 crore of additional revenue recognition potential, though the debt rise to Rs 1,118 crore is the offset.

rows.label: Net debt/equity rising toward 0.51 with a 0.75 ceiling
rows.why: Net debt rose to Rs 761 crore (ratio about 0.51 from 0.29), and management expects no more than about Rs 250 crore of further net debt additions before March 2027 with a 0.75 comfort ceiling.

rows.label: Mumbai/MMR entry via new project transactions
rows.why: Management is evaluating several MMR micro markets and expects transactions to be signed this quarter or next, while 8-9 million sq ft (about Rs 7,500-8,000 crore GDV) is at documentation stage with 21 projects under evaluation.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, sales momentum, cash flow and the H2 handover pipeline, but cautious on the FY28 target (dropped from the deck and reinstated verbally) and inconsistent on FY27 revenue and margin figures; analysts pressed on the JV economics, debt rise and FY28 targets.
